result.title: MemTrace: State-Consistent Memory for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
result.summary: As coding agents take on long-horizon software evolution tasks spanning multiple files and stages, longer execution trajectories introduce two coupled challenges: (1) accumulated histories strain context budgets, and (2) repository changes can invalidate earlier execution evidence. Existing approaches address these challenges through techniques like larger context windows, compression, retrieval, or repository representations, but often fail to reconstruct a consistent task state after a context refresh or verify whether recalled evidence remains valid. Thus, we introduce MemTrace, a provenance-aware memory system that preserves execution history and aligns its reuse with the evolving task (e.g., iterative cross-file repair) and repository state. MemTrace stores history as immutable Memory Traces anchored to key information (e.g., files, symbols, tests), and organizes their execution order and dependencies in a Memory Trace Graph. When context is constrained, working memory retains only compact Memory Anchors, from which the agent can reconstruct the latest execution state and locate evidence relevant to its next action. Before restoring historical evidence, MemTrace checks its validity against the current repository state and retrieves only what the next action requires. Across three complementary long-horizon coding benchmarks, MemTrace consistently outperforms all fully evaluated baselines under the same backbone and harness, improving DeepSWE pass@1 by 21.2 points, SWE-EVO Resolved Rate by 4.4 points, and SWE-Milestone Score by 17.8 points under Codex CLI.

AI.brief_summary: MemTrace 面向长周期代码演化智能体，提出一种带来源追踪的记忆系统：把执行历史存为锚定于文件、符号、测试的不可变 Memory Traces，并用 Memory Trace Graph 组织执行顺序与依赖，在上下文受限时只保留紧凑 Memory Anchors，恢复证据前先对照当前仓库状态校验有效性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态一致性校验 + 按需检索证据」的机制可能为 LVR 的视觉证据筛选、缓存失效判别与 LOOK/STOP 决策提供可核查线索，但它面向代码智能体、不涉及视觉 latent 状态，迁移需自行验证。
